findings.reason: the node should extend `ensure_remote_environment` (or reuse it as the check body) rather than fork the probe, and must resolve the return-shape mismatch before it can implement the check.
findings.text: `ensure_remote_environment` already owns the facility remote-environment need: it calls `probe_remote_environment` (remote/tools.py:550) and is invoked by the SSH stages (`imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py:172`, `imas_codex/cli/discover/code.py:186`). §2 says an uncovered need "is added to the monitor as a check through `probe_remote_environment` … never probed beside it", but that adds a second probe path beside this existing owner and does not name it; `probe_remote_environment` also returns a status dict, not the `(healthy: bool, detail: str)` tuple `ServiceMonitor.add_check` requires (services.py:856–887), so the proposed check is not constructible as described.

findings.reason: the census changes the node's shape from "promote two privates" to "delete one duplicate and route both call sites at base/image.py", which is the honest change the item exists to force.
findings.text: §2 states documents has its pending checks "only as private helpers" and proposes one public `has_pending_work` replacing them, but the image-score half already has a public owner: `has_pending_image_work` (imas_codex/discovery/base/image.py:354), re-exported at `imas_codex/discovery/wiki/graph_ops.py:1977`. `_has_pending_image_scores` (pipeline.py:74) duplicates that query. The plan would create a third predicate over the same `Image` state rather than consolidating onto base/image.py.

findings.reason: the plan should state that the runner's pre-stage re-probe is the only probe, or extend the harness's `extra_service_checks` (common.py:157, 268) so the stage and the runner share one monitor; otherwise the "one owner" claim is false and SSH is probed twice per stage.
findings.text: §2 asserts "one owner holds facility access", but the runner's `ServiceMonitor` is a second lifecycle beside the one every stage builds when invoked: each stage command calls `run_discovery` (common.py:212), which constructs its own monitor via `create_discovery_monitor` (common.py:502). The plan re-probes "each SSH or tunnel need again just before its stage runs" while the invoked stage (signals.py:172, code.py:186) probes the same need again inside its own harness.

findings.reason: the section must account for the added option surface in its own text — retiring, merging, or stating why nothing can be — and resolve the `--cost-limit` meaning clash before the option is implemented.
findings.text: supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §3 adds the `discover run` command and options `--dry-run`, `--only`, `--skip`, `--time`, `--cost-limit` and `--through mapping`, and re-declares `--cost-limit` and `--time` that every per-domain command already owns (`imas_codex/cli/discover/signals.py:26,83`, `wiki.py:21,66`, `documents.py:30,65`, `map.py:47,61`, `code.py:46,93`, `paths.py:28,99`, `imas_codex/cli/map.py:120,137`). §3 says only "adds one CLI entry and retires none"; it does not name the option family it adds or say why none of it can be merged. (`--cost-limit` at the sequence level also carries a different meaning — a shared total split proportionally — from the per-stage cap of the same name, an overload the section does not address.)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — `sequence.py` hides stage ordering, access gating, per-stage re-probe, cost splitting and the run report behind one command; the registry is data and the runner is one loop, so the module is not a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements facility-access probing and the image pending-work check beside owners that already exist (`ensure_remote_environment` common.py:443; `has_pending_image_work` base/image.py:354), and stands up a second `ServiceMonitor` lifecycle beside the one each stage already builds.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §2's one added public definition is accounted for in its own text ("one added public definition, which replaces two private ones"), but §3 adds the `discover run` command and the `--dry-run`/`--only`/`--skip`/`--time`/`--cost-limit`/`--through` option family, re-declaring a `--cost-limit` and `--time` that every per-domain command already owns, without naming what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanisms it extends (`DISCOVERY_DOMAINS` common.py:30, `ServiceMonitor` services.py:830 and its `neo4j_health_check`/`ssh_health_check`/`wiki_auth_check`, `create_discovery_monitor` common.py:502, `run_discovery` common.py:212, and the six per-domain pending-work predicates), so its reuse map is demonstrably populated; the two owners it missed are carried under `duplicate_owner`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3 states why the runner invokes each stage command whole (`ctx.invoke`) rather than refactoring the seven commands or spawning subprocesses; that is the justification the item asks for. The un-justified part is the re-declared option surface, carried under `interface_budget`.
